analysis_steps.goal: Derive mass loss rates for the SEO and NEO fragments from 13CO(3-2) flux

method.value: Calculate mass per unit radius M_R from optically thin 13CO(3-2) flux per unit radius F_R using level population and molecular constants, then multiply by projected radial wind velocity V_R: M_dot = M_R * V_R.

evidence.quote: To do so we measure its mean mass $M_R$ per unit of $R$ and its radial velocity $V_R$ projected on the plane of the sky, the mass loss rate being the product of these two quantities: $\dot{M}=M_R \times V_R$.

The relation between the total emission ($F$) and the number of molecules ($N$) is $F=hc/(4\pi d^2)NA_{ji}f_{pop}$ where $h$ is Planck constant, $c$ the velocity of light, $d$ the distance to the Earth, $A_{ji}$ the Einstein coefficients and $f_{pop}=(2J+1)\exp(-E_u/T)/(T/2.7)$ the population of $^{13}$CO at level $J$.

key_parameters.value: A_ji = 2.18e-6 s^-1, E_u = 31.7 K for 13CO(3-2); V_R(SEO) = 3.0+-0.5 km s^-1; V_R(NEO) = 2.9+-0.8 km s^-1; radial extension 1.0+-0.2 arcsec (SEO) and 1.5+-0.3 arcsec (NEO)

findings_qualitative.value: Dense gas is confined within ~50 au of Mira A, with broad SiO(5-4) line widths (>20 km s^-1) within 15 au driven by pulsation and convective cell shocks, and possible slow rotation within 15 au.

evidence.quote: we give evidence for confinement and probably rotation of a dense gas volume within $\sim$50 au from the star and for a large SiO line-width within $\sim$15 au.

findings_qualitative.value: Mass loss in Mira A is episodic and fragmented: SWO and NEA are detached fragments emitted decades ago, while current mass loss proceeds toward the blue hemisphere via SEO, NEO, and SWS.

evidence.quote: the presence of two fragments, SWO and NEA, emitted a few decades ago and nearly detached from the central gas reservoir, giving additional evidence for the episodic nature of the mass loss
the current mass loss proceeding toward the blue-shifted hemisphere along three favored directions: the SEO, dominated by the wind focused by Mira B, the NEO and the SWS

findings_qualitative.value: Outside the south-western quadrant, the SiO/CO abundance ratio is ~0.5-1x10^-4, at least two orders of magnitude lower than in similar O-rich AGB stars (RS Cnc, EP Aqr), likely due to dust grain depletion and UV photo-dissociation.

evidence.quote: an evaluation of the SiO/CO abundance ratio at the level of 0.5-1$\times$10$^{-4}$ when excluding the south-western quadrant, at least two orders of magnitude smaller than other typical low mass-loss-rate oxygen-rich AGB stars, and a possible interpretation in terms of the combined effect of depletion on dust grains and photo-dissociation by interstellar UV radiation.

findings_qualitative.value: The strong SiO emission in the south-western quadrant is anti-correlated with CO and is likely caused by the 2003 mass ejection / X-ray burst shock outgassing SiO from dust or recombining UV-dissociated SiO, rather than nascent wind generation.

evidence.quote: We argue that the SiO emission observed in the south-western quadrant is not related to the mechanism of generation of the nascent wind but to a mass ejection that occurred eleven years before the observations.

claims.hypothesis: The broad SiO(5-4) line width within 15 au of Mira A is due to local shock-induced turbulence rather than a large-scale velocity gradient such as rotation, although weak rotation may still be present.
claims.experiment: Measured full-width at 1/5 maximum of SiO(5-4) spectra in concentric rings (25-215 mas), re-centered spectra in each 30x30 mas^2 pixel on its mean velocity to remove velocity gradients, and fitted a sine wave to <V_z> vs position angle omega in the 30-100 mas ring.
claims.result: Line width decreases from 21 to 7 km s^-1 from 50 to 150 mas; pixel re-centering reduces rms deviation by at most 0.1 km s^-1 (0.05 km s^-1 on average); sine wave fits yield a projected rotation velocity of 0.7+-0.2 km s^-1 around an axis at PA 40+-15 deg.
claims.finding: The broad line width (>20 km s^-1 at R < 50 mas) is intrinsic and caused by pulsation/convection shocks, while a weak rotation of 0.7+-0.2 km s^-1 is probably present within 15 au.

evidence.loc: SiO(5-4) line width in the 5 to 15 au range
evidence.quote: The decrease of the rms deviation with respect to the mean never exceeds 0.1 km s$^{-1}$ and, on average, is only 0.05 km s$^{-1}$.

evidence.loc: SiO(5-4) line width in the 5 to 15 au range
evidence.quote: The sine wave fits suggest the presence of rotation within some 15 au from the center of the star with a projected velocity of 0.7$\pm$0.2 km s$^{-1}$ about an axis projecting 40$^\circ$$\pm$15$^\circ$ east of north.

claims.hypothesis: The mass loss of Mira A is episodic and fragmented rather than steady and spherically symmetric, leading to a current mass loss rate near the star that differs from single-dish averages.
claims.experiment: Analyzed optically thin 13CO(3-2) position-velocity maps in rotated coordinates (x', y') within |V_z| < 4 km s^-1, identified kinematic components, and calculated mass loss rates for ongoing outflows (SEO, NEO) from 13CO flux and projected wind velocities.
claims.result: NEA and SWO are detached from the central reservoir, whereas SEO, NEO, and SWS are connected; SEO and NEO have mass loss rates of (3.9+-1.7)x10^-8 and (2.7+-1.0)x10^-8 M_sun yr^-1, totaling (6.6+-2.0)x10^-8 M_sun yr^-1 (~10^-7 M_sun yr^-1 including SWS), or ~30-50% of single-dish values.
claims.finding: Mass loss proceeds via episodic, anisotropic fragments modulated over decades; current ongoing mass loss flows into the blue hemisphere at ~10^-7 M_sun yr^-1.

evidence.quote: Another advantage of this representation is to make it clear that the NEA and the SWO are nearly detached from the central emission: they are associated with masses of gas that have been emitted several decades ago. In contrast, the NEO and SWS are in continuity with the central emission and are therefore associated with on-going mass loss.

Adding together the contributions of the SEO and NEO, we obtain a mass loss rate of (6.6$\pm$2.0)$\times$10$^{-8}$ M$_\odot$yr$^{-1}$, accounting for $\sim$30% of the mass loss rate obtained from single dish observations

claims.hypothesis: Outside the south-western quadrant, the fragments of Mira A's wind are strongly depleted in gas-phase SiO compared to other oxygen-rich AGB stars due to dust condensation and UV photo-dissociation.
claims.experiment: Measured SiO(5-4) and 13CO(3-2) fluxes in region C fragments outside the SW quadrant, derived the SiO/12CO abundance ratio in the optically thin limit, and compared radial profiles of SiO(5-4)/CO(3-2) with RS Cnc and EP Aqr.
claims.result: SiO(5-4)/13CO(3-2) intensity ratio is ~0.1, corresponding to an SiO/12CO abundance ratio of 6.3x10^-5 (0.5-1x10^-4); beyond 100 au, SiO(5-4)/12CO(3-2) is ~0.005 for Mira vs ~0.6 for RS Cnc and ~1.2 for EP Aqr.
claims.finding: Gas-phase SiO outside the SW quadrant is present in the CO fragments but suppressed by at least two orders of magnitude relative to similar O-rich AGB stars, consistent with depletion onto dust and rapid UV photo-dissociation in low-density fragments.

evidence.loc: Confinement at short distances of the SiO emissions outside the south-western quadrant
evidence.quote: The ratio between the SiO(5-4) and $^{12}$CO(3-2) intensities beyond 100 au and excluding the south-western quadrant is therefore $\sim$0.005, consistent with our 0.1 estimate for the SiO(5-4)/$^{13}$CO(3-2) ratio from Table 3. In comparison, at similar distances, the SiO(5-4)/$^{12}$CO(3-2) ratio is $\sim$0.6 for RS Cnc and $\sim$1.2 for EP Aqr.

an evaluation of the SiO/CO abundance ratio at the level of 0.5-1$\times$10$^{-4}$ when excluding the south-western quadrant, at least two orders of magnitude smaller than other typical low mass-loss-rate oxygen-rich AGB stars, and a possible interpretation in terms of the combined effect of depletion on dust grains and photo-dissociation by interstellar UV radiation.

claims.hypothesis: The strong SiO(5-4) emission in the south-western quadrant is caused by the 2003 mass ejection / X-ray outburst shock wave outgassing or recombining SiO in the pre-existing SWO, rather than nascent wind generation.
claims.experiment: Compared high-resolution SiO(5-4), 13CO(3-2), and 12CO(3-2) PV maps and radial profiles in the south-western quadrant between R = 1 and 3 arcsec.
claims.result: CO and SiO emissions are strongly anti-correlated in the SW quadrant: CO is depressed toward the west at V_z ~ -1.5+-0.5 km s^-1 where SiO shows a prominent stream and broad component.
claims.finding: The 2003 ejection scenario qualitatively accounts for the CO hole and enhanced SiO emission, decoupling the SW quadrant anomaly from the nascent wind mechanism, though quantitative modeling is still required.

why_this_data.value: 13CO(3-2) has much smaller optical depth than 12CO(3-2), allowing finer morphological definition and direct molecule counting for mass loss rates, while high-resolution SiO(5-4) probes the inner 5-15 au shock/rotation zone and outer SiO depletion.

evidence.quote: In the present section, we take advantage of the smaller optical depth of the $^{13}$CO(3-2) observations to study the gas morphology in finer details than was possible using $^{12}$CO(3-2) observations.
We use the $^{13}$CO data to take advantage of the low line opacity: in the optically thin approximation, the total flux provides a direct measure of the number of molecules.

why_this_method.value: Limiting Doppler velocity to |V_z| < 4 km s^-1 isolates recent mass loss from ancient (>1000 yr) shells; rotating coordinates by 35 deg aligns with the symmetry axis of region C; integrating PV maps over the third dimension captures the full flux of 3D fragments.
